within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From multiplicativity to a sparse RH-sensitive witness set
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Prime-power multiplicativity creates a hierarchy of normalized extremizers whose tuned small-prime factorizations concentrate the divisor-sum fluctuations capable of witnessing failure of the RH criterion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The fluctuation transfer is explicitly heuristic here, and the decisive thin-set witness statement is imported from Robin rather than proved in Section 2.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Three scales isolate the RH-sensitive boundary
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Average behavior is too small to probe RH, maximal behavior reaches the Mertens/Robin scale, and only small fluctuations around that extremal boundary can change the criterion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source states the average, maximal, and unconditional refined bounds from prior work; it does not derive their full asymptotics locally.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Exceptional ties link transcendence to extremal factorization jumps
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The parameterized exponent shape is stable on generic intervals, while equality between competing prime contributions produces discrete tie parameters whose possible multiplicity is constrained by rational-power phenomena.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The Alaoglu-Erdos rational-power assertion and the four-exponentials conjecture are unresolved, so the claimed exclusion of four-way ties is conditional.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The elementary criterion is a two-sided threshold sandwich
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The harmonic expression is chosen to sit strictly above Robin's RH-true threshold yet below the infinitely-often RH-false excess for large inputs, converting an analytic dichotomy into an elementary universal inequality plus a finite initial check.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The equivalence remains dependent on Robin's external theorems, the finite computation is reported without a certificate here, and the upper-bridge display needs scan verification before exact reuse.
